subject: Life Skills
title: Buffer Time Is Not Wasted Time
description: One-minute skill: Buffer Time Is Not Wasted Time.

hook.text: She scheduled meetings back-to-back all day. By 3 PM she had no notes, no follow-ups, and no mental clarity.

buildup.text: Buffer time is the space between tasks where processing happens. Without it, context never gets absorbed.

discovery.text: Fifteen minutes between meetings lets you debrief, jot next steps, and mentally prepare for the next topic.

twist.text: Ambitious people see buffers as slack. In reality, removing them causes a quality collapse by mid-afternoon.

climax.text: Default your calendar to 25-minute or 50-minute meetings. The gap builds itself into every transition.

punchline.text: Margin is not laziness. It is infrastructure.

quiz.question: Why are buffers between tasks important?
options: They give you time to check social media
They allow processing, note-taking, and mental transition
They make your schedule look less intimidating
